app.title: Load Curve & Solar Sizing
app.description: Estimate how much energy a home, business or building uses hour by hour, and size the solar system that could supply it.

hero.title: How much energy does your place use, and when?
hero.empty: Add your loads and this skyline takes the shape of your day.
hero.aria: Hourly consumption drawn as a city skyline. Highest {peak} at {peak_hour}, lowest {base} at {base_hour}.
hero.aria_empty: An empty city skyline under a 24-hour sky, waiting for your loads.

loads.title: Your loads
loads.lede: List each piece of equipment, its power and the hours it is on.
loads.empty: Start with the sample office or import your spreadsheet.
loads.note: Click or drag across the hours each load is on. Use % is the share of those hours it actually draws power: a fridge compressor runs about 40% of the time, a light 100%.
loads.replace_confirm: Replace the current loads with the ones in this file?
loads.issues_title: {count} rows were skipped. Fix them in the file and import it again:

day.title: Day and seasons
day.lede: Choose which hours count as day and how consumption changes through the year.
day.strip: Day from {start} to {end}; the other hours count as night.
day.seasons_lede: 100% is a typical month. Raise the months you use more energy, such as 130% when the air conditioning runs all summer.

location.title: Location
location.lede: Look up how much sun your location gets, or enter peak sun hours by hand.
location.hint: Decimal degrees, as a map shows them: south and west are negative.
location.loading: Asking PVGIS for this location's sun hours…
location.average: On average, {hours} peak sun hours a day.
location.from_pvgis: From PVGIS. Best panel tilt: {slope}°, azimuth {azimuth}° (0° faces south, 180° faces north).

results.title: Your consumption
results.lede: When you use energy matters as much as how much: night-time energy has to come from the grid or a battery.
results.empty: Your charts appear here once you add a load.
results.year: In a year: {total} ({day} by day, {night} at night).
results.hourly_caption: Average power in each hour of a typical day. Sunflower bars are daytime hours; lavender bars are night-time hours.
results.hourly_aria: Bar chart of power for each hour of the day. Highest: {peak} at {hour}.
results.duration_caption: The same 24 hours sorted from highest to lowest power: how many hours a day you need at least that much. A flat curve means steady consumption.
results.hours_at_or_above: Hours a day at or above this power
results.monthly_caption: Energy each month after its seasonal multiplier, split into day and night.
results.monthly_aria: Stacked bar chart of energy per month. Total per year: {total}.
results.heatmap_caption: Each row is a load, each column an hour; the darker the cell, the more power it draws.

systems.title: Solar systems
systems.lede: On-grid, hybrid and off-grid systems sized for your consumption, side by side.
systems.empty: Add your loads and a location to size the systems.
systems.on_grid_hint: Connected to the grid, no batteries
systems.hybrid_hint: Grid plus batteries for the night
systems.need_sun: Add your location or type the sun hours in step 3 to size the systems.
systems.verdict: To run the night on batteries you need about {hybrid} kWh of storage; leaving the grid entirely takes about {extra} kWh more.
systems.verdict_no_off_grid: To run the night on batteries you need about {hybrid} kWh of storage. An off-grid system is not possible here.
systems.not_feasible: Not possible here: a month with consumption gets no sun, so no battery bank could be recharged.
systems.how_intro: The classic peak-sun-hours method. Each line shows the formula, then the same formula with your numbers.
systems.assumptions_intro: Typical values for a modern installation. Change them if your equipment or supplier says otherwise.
systems.f_array_on_grid: Energy per day to cover ÷ (peak sun hours × performance ratio), on yearly averages.
systems.f_array_hybrid: (Day energy + night energy ÷ battery efficiency) ÷ (peak sun hours × performance ratio), on yearly averages.
systems.f_array_off_grid: (Day energy + night energy ÷ battery efficiency) ÷ (peak sun hours × performance ratio), in the critical month: the one with the least sun for its consumption.
systems.f_panels_generic: Array power × 1000 ÷ panel power, rounded up.
systems.f_battery_hybrid: Night energy of the busiest month ÷ (depth of discharge × battery efficiency).
systems.f_battery_off_grid: Daily energy of the busiest month × days of autonomy ÷ (depth of discharge × battery efficiency).
systems.f_inverter_on_grid: The installed array power: the grid serves the peaks of your loads.
systems.f_inverter_load: Highest hourly power of the year × safety factor.

footer.data: Solar data from PVGIS, European Commission Joint Research Centre.
footer.disclaimer: These are estimates: confirm them with an installer before buying equipment.

errors.network: The server did not answer. Check your connection and try again.
errors.string_too_long: Use a shorter name (80 characters at most).
errors.greater_than_equal: Enter a number of at least {limit}.
errors.less_than_equal: Enter a number of at most {limit}.
errors.literal_error: Use 1 for on and 0 for off.
errors.duplicate_load_name: Two loads share this name. Give each load its own name.
errors.empty_daytime_window: Day must start and end at different hours.
errors.no_solar_resource: At least one month needs sun hours above zero.
errors.unsupported_file_type: Use a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file.
errors.unreadable_file: This file could not be read. Save it again as CSV or .xlsx and retry.
errors.missing_columns: The file is missing these columns: {columns}. Download the template to see the expected layout.
errors.too_many_rows: The file has more than 500 loads. Split it into smaller studies.
errors.file_too_large: The file is larger than 1 MB.
errors.location_over_sea: That point is over the sea. Pick a location on land.
errors.invalid_location: PVGIS has no data for that point. Check the coordinates.
errors.pvgis_unavailable: PVGIS is not answering right now. Try again, or enter peak sun hours by hand.
errors.pvgis_unexpected_response: PVGIS sent data this tool cannot read. Enter peak sun hours by hand.
errors.coordinates_out_of_range: Enter a latitude between -90 and 90 and a longitude between -180 and 180.
errors.geolocation_denied: Your browser did not share your location. Type the coordinates instead.
errors.study_file_invalid: This file is not a study saved by this tool.
errors.study_file_newer: This study was saved by a newer version of the tool and cannot be opened here.
